title: `referenceTo` column override: promised in the README, kept by nothing — make the promise real or withdraw it (enforce-or-remove, from #6425)
body:
Provenance: maintainer ruling 2026-08-27 (PM chat, decision-inbox batch 6, adjudication session `session_01DKWDdUJ2XNRESVVWUvcpnh`) on #6425's per-key disposition: `referenceTo` is ⛔ NOT declared as currently spelled — it is the "promised but not kept" key, split out to the enforce-or-remove channel as its own card.

## The measured state (from #6425's post-merge census, re-verify on the day)

- The README documents `referenceTo` as an author-facing column override.
- No consumer reads it: the consumers read `reference_to` / `reference` (a SPELLING mismatch, not an unused concept). Removing the key from a column changes nothing in any render — measured identical.
- Declaring it as-spelled on `TableColumn` would publish a promise that does nothing (the one option the ruling forbids).

## The two honest routes (measure first, then take the cheaper honest one)

1. **Enforce** — fix the spelling chain so the promise becomes real (the column override reaches the `reference_to`/`reference` readers). Take this only if measurement shows a real authoring story for a column-level reference override.
2. **Remove** — withdraw the README line (and the key from `AuthoredColumnOverrides`' held band, marking the verdict). Under the maintainer's standing startup-stage rule (2026-08-27: deprecated/alias spellings retire immediately, no transition windows), this is the lean default when no demand is measured.

⛔ Stop-and-report if enforcing would widen behaviour beyond making the documented override work as documented.

Named reader: the `domain:ui` execution seat. Refs: #6425 (the per-key ruling + census), PR #6590 (the read-side keyhole where the held verdict lives).
